cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, and the directions are a little strange. Tell the people to turn back and camp by the sea, near Pi-hahiroth. Right by the water, directly across from Baal-zephon.

cards.question: The LORD says Pharaoh will look at Israel's camp by the sea and think something about them. What?

cards.text: Then God says He'll harden Pharaoh's heart so Pharaoh will chase them. And Israel does exactly what God said.

cards.question: God says He'll gain honor through Pharaoh and all his army, and the Egyptians will ___ that He is the LORD.

cards.text: Back in Egypt, the king gets word that the people have fled. And Pharaoh and his officials change their minds.

cards.question: What do Pharaoh and his officials suddenly realize after Israel leaves?

answers.text: Their gods had let them down

cards.text: Picture a boss who signs off on your two weeks' notice, then realizes nobody else knows how the copier works. Pharaoh gets his chariot ready and takes his army, and his 600 best chariots are just the START.

cards.question: Pharaoh leaves every chariot in Egypt behind except his 600 best ones.

cards.text: The LORD hardens Pharaoh's heart, just like He said. Pharaoh chases Israel and catches up with them camped by the sea.

cards.question: The Israelites look up and see the Egyptians marching after them. What do they do?

answers.text: Cry out to the LORD in terror
Line up to fight the army

cards.text: Then they turn on Moses: "Was it because there were no graves in Egypt that you brought us into the wilderness to die?" Whoo, they did NOT ease into that one.

cards.question: The people tell Moses it would have been better to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.

cards.text: Moses answers, "Do not be afraid." Friend, I held my breath every time that drawer opened, and I think Moses is calmer with a whole ARMY coming.

cards.question: Moses tells the people to stand firm and see the LORD's salvation, and he says the Egyptians they see today, they will never see again.
Moses says the LORD will ___ for them, and they need only to be ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Moses, "Tell the Israelites to go forward." Friend, forward is the SEA.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Moses to do with his staff and his hand?

answers.text: Stretch it over the sea to divide it
Strike the rock to bring out water
Throw it down in front of Pharaoh

cards.question: God says the Israelites will go through the sea on ___ ground.

cards.text: God says He'll harden the Egyptians' hearts so they follow Israel right in, and they'll know that He is the LORD. Then the angel of God and the pillar of cloud, both going ahead of Israel's camp, start to move.

cards.question: The angel of God and the pillar of cloud move from in front of Israel's camp to behind it.

cards.text: The cloud stands between Egypt's camp and Israel's, there in the darkness, and it lights up the night. After all my years in a dark drawer, friend, I would've begged to camp next to that cloud.

cards.question: All night long, Egypt's army closes in on Israel's camp.

cards.text: Moses stretches out his hand over the sea. And all that night, the LORD drives the sea back.

cards.question: What does the LORD use to drive the sea back all night?

cards.text: The sea turns into dry land, and the waters are divided. Israel walks right through the middle of the sea.

cards.question: The Israelites walk through on dry ground, with walls of ___ on their right and on their left.

cards.text: Friend, I spent years squeezed between the takeout menus in that junk drawer, and these folks are walking between WALLS OF WATER. Then here come all Pharaoh's horses, chariots and horsemen, right into the sea after them.
At morning watch, the LORD looks down on Egypt's army from the pillar of fire and cloud. He throws their camp into confusion.

cards.question: The LORD causes the Egyptians' chariot ___ to wobble, so they have difficulty driving.
The Egyptians want to flee, saying the LORD is fighting for Israel against Egypt.

cards.text: Now even the Egyptians are saying what Moses told Israel. At the LORD's word, Moses stretches his hand over the sea again, and at daybreak the sea goes back to normal.

cards.question: As the Egyptians retreat, the waters flow back over the army that chased Israel into the sea. How many of them survive?

cards.text: But Israel walked through the sea on dry ground. That day the LORD saved Israel from the hand of the Egyptians.

cards.question: When Israel sees the great power the LORD used over Egypt, the people fear the LORD and believe in Him and in His servant Moses.

cards.text: Then Moses and the Israelites sing a song to the LORD. Friend, the last time I sang, my oven timer went off early just to drown me out.

cards.question: The song opens, "I will sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted." Then it says what the LORD has done. What?

answers.text: Thrown horse and rider into the sea
Split the rock in the wilderness
Sent frogs over the land of Egypt

cards.text: Then the song gets personal: "The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation."

cards.question: Because the LORD has become his salvation, the singer says he will praise the LORD and exalt Him.

cards.text: The LORD is a warrior, the song says, and He cast Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea. The finest of his officers drowned in the Red Sea and sank like a stone.

cards.question: Now the song talks straight to God. What does it say has shattered the enemy?

cards.text: The song keeps going. God overthrew His adversaries by His great majesty, and His burning wrath consumed them like stubble.

cards.question: Then the song looks back at the waters standing up like a wall. What does it say piled the waters up?

answers.text: The blast of the LORD's nostrils
The stamp of the LORD's feet

cards.text: Then the song tells what the enemy declared: "I will pursue, I will overtake." Five I wills in one breath, friend, and I can't even get through one "I will clean the oven."

cards.question: Then the song answers all that bragging: God blew with His ___, and the sea covered them.
The song asks, "Who among the gods is like You, O LORD?" Its point is that some gods are just as great as He is.

cards.text: The song says the earth swallowed the enemy up. Then it looks ahead, to where God is taking His people.

cards.question: With loving devotion, the song says, God will lead the people He redeemed. Where will He guide them?

answers.text: To the banks of the Jordan
To the shores of the Great Sea

cards.text: Then the song names who will hear about all this: Philistia, Edom, Moab and Canaan.

cards.question: The song says the nations will hear what God did and come out to welcome Israel.

cards.text: Terror and dread will fall on them until God's people pass by. And God will bring His people in and plant them on the mountain of His inheritance.

cards.question: The song ends by saying the LORD will ___ forever and ever.

cards.text: Then Miriam the prophetess, Aaron's sister, takes a tambourine in her hand.

cards.question: Miriam starts to play. Who follows her with tambourines and dancing?

cards.text: And Miriam sings back to them: "Sing to the LORD, for He is highly exalted; the horse and rider He has thrown into the sea." Friend, I dance stuck to a gold base, and even I want to grab a tambourine.
